stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of Solvang's finding. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Most songbirds that breed in northern Europe migrate south each autumn along a single, consistent route.
• In 2022, ornithologist Henrik Solvang attached lightweight trackers to 30 garden warblers nesting near Trondheim, Norway.
• Solvang found that individual warblers used different routes in different years, sometimes shifting by more than 400 kilometers.
• Such route flexibility had previously been documented only in large birds, such as geese and storks.
choices: In 2022, Solvang attached lightweight trackers to 30 garden warblers that were nesting near Trondheim, Norway.
Solvang's garden warblers changed migration routes between years, a flexibility previously documented only in large birds.
Most songbirds that breed in northern Europe migrate south each autumn along a single, consistent route.
Some of the garden warblers that Solvang tracked shifted their migration routes by more than 400 kilometers.
explanation: The goal asks why Solvang's finding matters. The last note says why: this kind of flexibility had been seen only in large birds before. Choice B states the finding and includes that comparison, so you can see what makes it significant.

A.why: You picked a description of the study's method: who, how many birds, where. It never says what Solvang found or why that finding matters.

C.why: You picked the background note. It sets up a contrast but never mentions Solvang's finding, so it can't show that finding's significance.

D.why: You picked a striking fact without the comparison that makes it significant. A 400-kilometer shift matters only because such flexibility was previously known only in large birds, and this choice leaves that out.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the achievement of the county's program in reducing childhood lead poisoning. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices: Kestrel County once had one of the highest childhood lead-poisoning rates of any county in its state.

A.why: You picked the background problem. It describes the situation before the program and says nothing about what the program achieved.

B.why: You confused the program's activity with its outcome. Inspecting 9,000 homes is what the program did. The goal asks what it achieved in reducing lead poisoning, and this choice never mentions lead-poisoning rates.

C.why: You accepted an exaggeration. The notes describe a 78 percent drop in one county, not the elimination of lead poisoning across the whole state.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of Haldorsen's fossils. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices: The fossil leaves Haldorsen examined have the net-like vein pattern that is typical of flowering plants.
Dated to 165 million years ago, Haldorsen's fossils could push back the origin of flowering plants by 35 million years.
Haldorsen dated the fossil leaves, which came from a quarry in Greenland, to about 165 million years ago.
Haldorsen's fossil leaves prove that flowering plants first evolved in Greenland 165 million years ago.

A.why: You picked a description of what the fossils look like. The vein pattern identifies them as flowering plants but doesn't say why they matter.

C.why: You picked a bare date. '165 million years ago' is significant only next to the long-held 130-million-year estimate, and this choice leaves that comparison out.

D.why: You accepted claims stronger than the evidence. The notes say the fossils would change the timeline only if confirmed, so 'prove' goes too far. Nothing in the notes says flowering plants first evolved in Greenland.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of Brandvold's find. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Seeds enclosed in a protective fruit wall are a defining trait of flowering plants.
• Most researchers had dated the earliest fruit-bearing plants to about 130 million years ago.
• In 2021, paleobotanist Ilse Brandvold examined fossils from the Velde Quarry in Norway.
• The fossils belong to a small shrub, which she named Veldea minor, whose seeds are enclosed in a fruit wall.
• The rock containing the fossils is about 152 million years old.
choices: In 2021, paleobotanist Ilse Brandvold examined fossils from Norway's Velde Quarry, including those of a small shrub with enclosed seeds that she named Veldea minor.
The fossilized shrub Veldea minor, whose seeds are enclosed in a fruit wall, was found in Norwegian rock that geologists have dated to about 152 million years ago.
Veldea minor, whose seeds sit inside a fruit wall, lived about 152 million years ago, roughly 20 million years before most researchers had thought fruit-bearing plants appeared.
Because its seeds sit inside a fruit wall, the 152-million-year-old Veldea minor shows that flowering plants first evolved in northern Europe and spread from there.
explanation: The goal asks why the find matters. The age of 152 million years only matters once you set it against the earlier estimate of 130 million years. Choice C makes that comparison: Veldea minor, a plant with seeds inside a fruit wall, is about 20 million years older than researchers believed such plants were. That states the significance outright instead of leaving you to work it out.

A.why: This choice tells you who examined the fossils, when, and where. It is accurate, but it never says why the find matters. You picked a description of the event when the goal asked for its importance.

B.why: This is the bare-date trap. The figure of 152 million years sounds impressive, but it shows significance only when compared with the earlier 130-million-year estimate, and this choice leaves that comparison out. Check that a relative claim, such as 'earliest,' includes the thing it is being compared with.

D.why: The notes say nothing about where flowering plants first evolved or how they spread. One fossil site can't show that. You picked a choice that makes the find sound important by claiming more than the notes support.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the achievement of Vasquez's plan. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• From 1968 to 2001, a six-lane elevated highway ran along the waterfront of Marlow Bay.
• In 1994, city planner Teodora Vasquez proposed replacing it with a surface boulevard and a public park.
• Critics predicted that removing the highway would cause severe traffic congestion downtown.
• The highway was torn down in 2001, and the new Harbor Promenade opened in 2004.
• A decade later, downtown traffic delays were no worse than before, and the number of people living near the waterfront had tripled.
choices: In 1994, city planner Teodora Vasquez proposed that Marlow Bay replace its six-lane elevated waterfront highway with a surface boulevard and a public park.
Marlow Bay's elevated waterfront highway was torn down in 2001, and the Harbor Promenade, the boulevard and park Vasquez had proposed, opened in 2004.
Critics predicted that Vasquez's plan would cause severe congestion downtown, and a decade after the Harbor Promenade opened, traffic delays there had grown worse.
Although critics had predicted severe congestion, a decade after Vasquez's boulevard replaced the highway, downtown traffic delays were no worse and waterfront residents had tripled.
explanation: An achievement is a result, and this one is impressive because it proved the critics wrong. Choice D sets the critics' prediction of severe congestion against what actually happened. Traffic delays did not get worse, and the number of people living near the waterfront tripled. The word 'although' names that contrast directly, so the plan's success is clear.

A.why: This choice accurately says who proposed the plan and what it involved. It stops before any outcome, though, so nothing in it shows the plan succeeded. You picked what the plan was when the goal asked what it achieved.

B.why: This is the timeline trap. It describes the highway coming down and the promenade opening, but those events are only steps in the project. The achievement is in the results a decade later, and this choice leaves them out.

C.why: The notes say traffic delays were no worse than before, not that they grew worse. This choice reverses the key result. It also turns the goal upside down, because it makes the plan look like a failure instead of an achievement.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of the trial's result. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices: Daria Okonkwo-Lind's 2024 trial of an experimental nasal-spray vaccine enrolled 412 adults at three separate clinics.

A single dose of the nasal-spray vaccine produced protective antibody levels in 88% of the 412 trial participants.
The nasal-spray vaccine protected 85% of participants after two doses, matching the standard injected vaccine's rate.

A.why: You picked a choice that tells who ran the trial, when, and how large it was. All of that is accurate, but it never mentions the result, so it can't show why the result matters.

C.why: You went with the bare figure. On its own, 88% after one dose doesn't tell a reader anything is remarkable. It only stands out next to the standard vaccine's 85% after two doses, and this choice drops that comparison.

D.why: You mixed up the two vaccines. The 85% rate after two doses belongs to the standard injected vaccine. The nasal spray reached 88% after one dose.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of Marsh's findings. All of the following choices use relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal EXCEPT:
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Sports scientists have long believed that heat acclimation benefits only athletes who compete in hot conditions.
• In 2019, physiologist Lena Marsh had 24 cyclists train for ten days in a 38°C heat chamber.
• She then tested the cyclists' power output in cool conditions (13°C).
• Their power output rose by an average of 6%, a gain comparable to that from altitude training.
• Marsh's study was among the first to show that heat training improves performance in cool weather.
choices: Marsh's study challenged a long-held belief: heat acclimation, thought to help only athletes competing in heat, also raised cyclists' power in cool conditions.
Marsh's study was among the first to show that ten days of heat training could improve cyclists' performance in cool weather, not just hot.
In 2019, Marsh had 24 cyclists train for ten days in a 38°C heat chamber and then tested their power output at 13°C.
After heat training, Marsh's cyclists raised their cool-weather power output by 6%, a gain comparable to that from altitude training.
explanation: The goal is to show why Marsh's findings matter, and choice C never does. It sets out the method accurately (the year, the number of cyclists, the chamber temperature, the test temperature) but doesn't give a result or any reason the study was important. This is the subtype's trap: an accurate description of the event with no significance. Each of the other three choices gives a reason it matters: it overturned an old belief, it was among the first of its kind, or its gain matched altitude training.

A.why: You may have thought 'challenged a long-held belief' claims more than the notes support. The first note states the belief, and Marsh's result contradicts it. Setting the finding against that background is exactly how a sentence shows significance.

B.why: You may have ruled this out because it leaves out the 6% figure and the details of the method. Using fewer notes doesn't make a choice fail. 'Among the first to show' is the note that says why the study matters, and this choice is built on it.

D.why: You may have read this as just a number. The 6% matters here because it is compared with altitude training, and the choice includes that comparison. The relative claim is what makes this a statement of significance.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of Halvorsen's map. All of the following choices use relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal EXCEPT:
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Through the early 1800s, mapmakers typically showed terrain with sketched hills, which conveyed a landscape's shape but not its exact height.
• Surveyor Margit Halvorsen spent six years measuring elevations across the Vessa Valley.
• Her 1838 map of the valley connected points of equal elevation with lines spaced every 20 meters.
• With these contour lines, readers could calculate the height of any point on the map.
• Contour lines did not become standard on national survey maps until decades later.
choices: Halvorsen's 1838 map of the Vessa Valley, the product of six years of surveying, connected points of equal elevation every 20 meters.
Halvorsen's 1838 map let readers calculate the height of any point, something the sketched hills common on maps of her era could not do.
Decades before contour lines became standard on national survey maps, Halvorsen's 1838 map used them to show the Vessa Valley's exact elevations.
Unlike the sketched hills on most early-1800s maps, which conveyed only a landscape's shape, Halvorsen's contour lines recorded exact heights.
explanation: Choice A describes the map: when it was made, how long the survey took, and how the lines were spaced. It never says why the map mattered. The date 1838 matters only when compared with when contour lines became standard, and A leaves that comparison out. Each of the other choices states the map's importance by comparing it with its background, either the sketched-hill maps of the time or the much later national survey maps.

B.why: You may have thought this only describes what readers could do with the map. It also compares that ability with the sketched hills of the era, which couldn't do it. That contrast is what makes this a statement of significance.

C.why: You may have suspected 'decades before' goes beyond the notes. The last note says contour lines became standard 'decades later.' This choice puts the date next to that comparison, which turns a bare date into a sign of how early the map was.

D.why: You may have dismissed this as a plain comparison rather than a statement of importance. Here the comparison is the significance. 'Unlike' marks how Halvorsen's map improved on the usual method, so the choice does what the goal asks.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the achievement of Reyna's footbridge. All of the following choices use relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal EXCEPT:
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Concrete footbridges in wet climates typically need crack repairs within ten years.
• In 2008, engineer Tomás Reyna built the Halden Creek footbridge from concrete containing bacteria that produce limestone.
• When rainwater seeps into a crack, the bacteria become active and seal it.
• The footbridge has now gone eighteen years without a single crack repair.
• It was among the first public structures built with self-healing concrete.
choices: Although concrete footbridges in wet climates typically need crack repairs within ten years, Reyna's self-healing bridge has needed none in eighteen.
One of the first public structures made of self-healing concrete, Reyna's footbridge has gone eighteen years without a single crack repair.
Reyna's footbridge has lasted eighteen years without repairs, nearly twice the span after which similar bridges typically need crack work.
Reyna's 2008 footbridge uses concrete containing bacteria that produce limestone, sealing cracks whenever rainwater seeps into them.
explanation: Choice D explains how the concrete works, with the bacteria, the limestone and the rainwater. It never says what the bridge achieved. This is the subtype's trap: an accurate account of what the thing is, with no outcome or importance. Each of the other choices states the achievement. Two compare the bridge's eighteen repair-free years with the usual ten, and one says it was among the first structures of its kind.

A.why: You may have read this as a simple contrast between two facts. The contrast is the achievement: 'although' marks that Reyna's bridge has far outlasted the typical repair timeline, which is exactly what the goal asks you to emphasize.

B.why: You may have thought eighteen years without repairs means little without the ten-year comparison. This choice gives a different reason it matters: the bridge was among the first of its kind. That alone accomplishes the goal.

C.why: You may have thought 'nearly twice' is a number the notes don't give. Eighteen years against a ten-year repair timeline is close to twice as long, so this is a fair way to state the comparison that shows the achievement.
